niche: a Medicaid managed care plan's 2026 cost per member-month for each primary care provider group, conformed from paid medical claims, the plan's monthly enrollment roster snapshots and the state's capitation remittance, where members who lapse at their annual renewal are reinstated retroactively and their lapse months never reach the roster
analyst_test: A strong analyst who conforms the claims, the roster and the remittance, reads every field and rule correctly and divides each group's paid claims by the member-months its monthly roster shows designates the wrong groups, because members who lapse at their annual renewal are reinstated retroactively, their lapse months never reach the roster though their claims in those months are paid, so the groups whose members churn most carry the most cost on the fewest roster months.
domain_test: The decisive quantity is each provider group's cost per member-month, a health plan's per-member-per-month rate whose denominator is the exposure at risk; under Medicaid renewal churn with retroactive reinstatement the covered months are rebuilt from the capitation the state paid and the claims the plan paid, not from the roster snapshot; swapping in another field's nouns breaks it because the annual redetermination cycle and the state's retroactive coverage rule are what put covered months outside the roster.
layer2_pattern: own:exposure at risk rebuilt from the payer's own retroactive capitation and paid claims under renewal churn
layer1: claims paid after the month of service, with claim lines and member IDs as the claims system writes them
the roster as a snapshot taken early each month
a remittance file paid by the state in a later month than the coverage month it pays
provider group attribution changes during the year
pharmacy claims reversed and rebilled under one claim number
stakeholder_role: the plan's provider performance analyst preparing the 2027 provider group designations

world.geography: United States, a fictional state's Medicaid program

driver: A rate's denominator is the time each member was covered, and members who lose coverage at a fixed yearly review and are restored back to the date they lost it never appear in the monthly snapshot of who is covered, though the payer's own later payments for them and the services it paid in those months record the coverage; the denominator is rebuilt from those payments rather than read off the snapshot.
driver_concrete: Each provider group's 2026 cost per member-month divides its attributed members' paid claims by member-months rebuilt from the plan's roster plus the months the state later paid capitation for after a renewal lapse, not by the roster's member-months alone, before groups above the plan's cost benchmark are designated.

differentiation.task127: task127 projects cost by tenure; here nothing is projected: a closed year's exposure is rebuilt from retroactive coverage the roster snapshot never shows.

lineage.driver: A unit's period total is measured hourly by an instrument that shares a utility with the unit's control device, so when the utility fails the instrument goes dark while the control is off; the dark hours are filled at the uncontrolled level the instrument reads in its first hours back, times the hour's metered input, rather than from the unit's measured hours in the same operating state or from the hours either side, which the controlled hours dominate.
lineage.stump: The default path fills every unmonitored hour from the unit's own measured hours in the same start state and load, and designates AF-2, CB-1, DF-1, DF-3 and SR-1; the gaps that came with the plants' instrument air trips are hours when the SCR's air-operated ammonia valves had closed as well, which the first measured hour after each trip shows at about twenty times the controlled rate, so filling those hours at that uncontrolled level adds CB-2 and AF-1.
lineage.fate: spent at stage 4 on 2026-10-20: reader 12 landed the call after the register's air-to-open grounding (1 of 6 readers since it went in; 11 of 12 overall missed); the asks' revision device held at 0 of 18 for both round-6 readers

lineage.driver: A unit's period total is measured hourly by an instrument that is out mostly in the hours after the unit starts, when the quantity runs several times its steady level at the same operating point, so the missing hours are filled by the hour's start state, read from an every-hour operating log, rather than by a fit on the operating point that the steady hours dominate.
lineage.stump: The default path fills each unmonitored hour from the unit's NOx-on-load regression and designates the units that run steadily high, because the analyzers drop out mostly right after a start, when the cold catalyst lets NOx run at several times the steady rate; filling the missing hours by hours since start designates the hard-cycling units the program should fund.
